title: Teen Swimmer Breaks a 23-Year-Old Record!
summary: Have you ever tried to hold your breath and swim as fast as you can? Imagine doing that while racing against the clock—and breaking a record that stood for 23 years! That's exactly what 17-year-old Sienna Toohey did at the Australian Swimming Trials. She swam the 100-meter breaststroke in just 1 minute and 5.97 seconds. That's super fast! The old record for a 17-year-old was set by Leisel Jones, one of the greatest swimmers ever, back in 2003. Leisel's time was 1:06.37. Sienna beat it by almost half a second. Sienna is from Albury, Australia. She had been getting close to the record earlier this year with a time of 1:06.43. But in this race, she exploded off the start and was ahead right from the first 50 meters. Her first half was so fast that no one could catch her. Now Sienna is the third-fastest Australian woman ever in this event. She's also the fastest Australian swimmer in the 100 breaststroke since the super-suit era ended. Super-suits were special swimsuits that helped swimmers go faster, but they were banned in 2010. So Sienna's time is extra impressive. If she keeps swimming like this, she could win medals at the Olympics or World Championships. Australia hasn't had a top swimmer in this event for years. Way to go, Sienna!
why_it_matters: Sienna shows that hard work and determination can help you achieve goals that seem impossible, and her story might inspire you never to give up on your own dreams, whether in sports, art, or school.

background_read: Australia is famous for producing world-class swimmers, like Ian Thorpe and Emma McKeon. The Australian Swimming Trials are where young talents earn their place on the national team.
Leisel Jones (an Australian swimming legend who won many Olympic medals) set the under‑18 record in 2003, and it took 23 years for someone to beat it.
The super-suit era was a short time around 2008 when special plastic-like swimsuits helped swimmers go much faster; after they were banned, records became harder to break.
Article_Structure: WHO: Sienna Toohey, a 17-year-old swimmer from Albury, Australia.
WHAT: She broke the 23-year-old Australian record for the 100-meter breaststroke in her age group.
WHERE: At the Australian Swimming Trials.
WHY: Because she trained hard and exploded off the start, swimming faster than any other Australian teenager ever in that event.

perspectives.description: Swimming lovers see Sienna as a new star who can bring medals back to Australia. Breaking a record set by a legend is a huge sign of talent.

Some people say it is just an age-group record, not a world record, so it might not be that special. Others wonder if super-suits make later records seem less impressive, even though Leisel Jones swam before that era.
Records are a way to measure how swimming has improved over time. Sienna’s time shows that young athletes keep getting faster, and this is a normal part of sport.
